record.paper_title: Constructing groups of 'small' order: Recent results and open problems
record.original_question: Let E3 be the set of integers n with 1 <= n <= 20000 such that 2^8 * p^2 divides n for p in {3, 5, 7}. For the orders in E3 other than the already determined exception n = 2^8 * 3^2 = 2304, can the solvable finite groups of order n be constructed or enumerated up to isomorphism, possibly by improving the Frattini extension method?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $\mathcal{E}_3$ denote the set of integers $n$ with $1 \le n \le 20000$ such that $n$ is divisible by $2^8 \cdot p^2$ for some prime $p \in \{3,5,7\}$. It is known that the finite solvable groups of order $n = 2^8 \cdot 3^2 = 2304$ have been constructed and enumerated up to isomorphism. For each of the remaining orders $n \in \mathcal{E}_3 \setminus \{2304\}$, determine whether one can effectively construct, up to isomorphism, a complete and irredundant list of all finite solvable groups of order $n$. In particular, develop (or identify the obstructions to) an improvement of the Frattini extension method — the algorithm that builds every finite solvable group of order $n$ as a Frattini extension of a Frattini-free group of order dividing $n$ by an elementary abelian normal subgroup contained in the Frattini subgroup — that is capable of completing this enumeration for every such $n$.
artifact.status_search_result: Available references on the Frattini extension method (Besche–Eick, GrpConst, Cubefree packages) and the SmallGroups library indicate that orders divisible by high powers of 2 (such as 2^8) remain computationally infeasible in general, and that constructing subdirect products is the principal bottleneck. No source located indicates that the solvable groups for all such orders in the specified range have been enumerated; the problem is presented as an outstanding computational challenge.

status_evidence.title: Constructing groups of 'small' order
status_evidence.snippet: discusses orders for which solvable groups cannot yet be constructed, including those with 2^8 dividing n
status_evidence.claim: The enumeration of solvable groups of these orders is identified as an open computational problem.

status_evidence.title: GrpConst - GAP packages
status_evidence.snippet: FrattiniExtensionMethod constructs all soluble groups of a given order
status_evidence.claim: The Frattini extension method is the current state of the art but is limited by subdirect product computation for high 2-power orders.

status_evidence.title: SmallGrp - The GAP Small Groups Library
status_evidence.claim: Order 2304 has been completed, consistent with it being the known exception.
